The provided text contrasts the thematic presentation of good versus evil in J.R.R. Tolkien's 'The Lord of the Rings' and C.S. Lewis's 'The Chronicles of Narnia'. Both works share the central theme of the conflict between good and evil. However, they differ in their approach to moral clarity. 'The Lord of the Rings' is described as having a clear distinction between the forces of good and darkness, whereas 'The Chronicles of Narnia' is noted for blurring this line by introducing characters who waver between sides, resulting in a more nuanced view of morality.
